bull.probability_evidence: Q3 2026 organic growth accelerated to 3.1% with 8% international growth, and PEP trades 46% below peer P/E/EV-EBITDA and below its own 5y multiple minimums (factsheet-2026-10-09.md Valuation table; 2026-10-09.md §3), but the macro overlay's small bear tilt (rising real 10y yield to 2.92%, +0.61pp/3m; firming dollar, DTWEXBGS 121.4, +2.86pts/1m) trims the odds of a fast re-rating toward peers (research/PEP/2026-10-09-macro.md, macro_tilt).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet base-row valuation anchors: DCF $144.31 vs P/E $207.00 (factsheet-2026-10-09.md Fair value table); half the $62.69 spread ($31.35) relative to the $165.21 target = 18.97%, within the inputs file's blended residual volatility cap of 19.8% (2026-10-09-mc-inputs.json regression.residual_vol.blended).

base.probability_evidence: Organic revenue growth of 3.1% in Q3 2026 (stockanalysis.com/stocks/pep/transcripts/706870-q3-2026/) exceeds the 0.8% the reverse DCF implies, but management says it is 'not satisfied' with U.S. performance and cut EPS guidance despite the revenue beat (2026-10-09.md §2-3; evaluation.md Bear case), supporting a move toward the DCF base value without a full P/E re-rating.

target_band.cite: Fact sheet base-row anchors DCF $144.31 vs P/E $207.00 (factsheet-2026-10-09.md Fair value table); half the $62.69 spread ($31.35) relative to the $144.31 target = 21.73%, capped at the inputs file's blended residual volatility of 19.8% (2026-10-09-mc-inputs.json regression.residual_vol.blended) since the uncapped figure exceeds it.

bear.probability_evidence: Q3 2026 U.S. soda volumes declined and TTM margins (operating 16.8%, FCF 10.7%) sit above FY2025 levels (8.2% FCF margin), so a reversion toward FY2025 levels plus the macro overlay's small bear tilt (real yields above 3.25%, dollar strength muting the 8% international growth offset) could drag the stock toward the bear fair value (2026-10-09.md §2-3; evaluation.md Bear case; research/PEP/2026-10-09-macro.md macro_bear).

jumps.reason: Quarterly earnings releases are a recurring source of guidance surprises for PEP; the Q3 2026 report (2026-10-08) produced an EPS guidance cut despite a revenue beat, on declining U.S. soda volumes and margin pressure, which investors are still digesting.
